## pplx-05 — GitHub Actions supply-chain hardening

- Tool: perplexity-web `search` · Date: 2026-09-27
- Query: "GitHub Actions supply chain hardening 2026: pinning actions to full commit SHA, top-level permissions read-all / contents: read, zizmor audit, pinact, Dependabot for github-actions, composer audit in CI — best practice checklist for PHP open source monorepo"
- Status: provenance.

## Answer (verbatim, condensed only by removing blank lines)

For a public PHP monorepo, treat workflow hardening as a set of enforceable gates—not just a convention to pin actions. Your proposed controls are a strong baseline, with two important refinements: use permissions: {} plus job-level grants where practical, and audit each Composer lockfile that represents a separately installable package.

Baseline checklist
- Pin every action and reusable workflow to a verified, full-length commit SHA. Keep a human-readable version comment beside the SHA, and verify the commit belongs to the upstream repository—not a fork. GitHub identifies full-SHA pinning as the immutable-reference option and supports policy enforcement for it.
- Set workflow permissions explicitly. Prefer permissions: {} at workflow level, then grant only what a job needs. If you choose permissions: read-all, understand that it grants read access across all permission scopes; it is broader than contents: read. For ordinary checkout-and-test jobs, contents: read is often enough.
- Run zizmor against workflow files and Dependabot configuration in CI. Make findings actionable: block on serious findings, document narrowly scoped exceptions, and review exceptions periodically.
- Use pinact to pin or update action references, but treat its changes as dependency updates: review the SHA, upstream repository, and version comment before merging.
- Enable Dependabot’s github-actions ecosystem at directory: "/" so it scans workflow files in .github/workflows.
- Run composer audit in CI against the committed lockfile for each independently installable Composer project. Composer’s audit --locked audits the lockfile, and audit failures should block merges unless a reviewed exception is justified.
Minimal permissions: `permissions: {}` at workflow level; `jobs.test.permissions: contents: read`.

Monorepo Composer coverage
- Inventory every composer.json; run composer validate --strict for each package root; composer audit --locked wherever a composer.lock is committed; do not assume a root-level audit covers nested packages; keep installation locked (composer install); separate "advisory" from "audit service failed" (Composer audit exit code 1 for policy matches).

Pull requests and release workflows
- Minimal permissions for fork PRs; no pull_request_target with fork code; separate protected release jobs; GitHub-hosted runners; CODEOWNERS for .github/workflows/**; org policy requiring full-SHA-pinned actions.

Maintenance
- Schedule Dependabot updates; zizmor findings beyond pinning; suppressions with reason/owner/re-review date; verify each new SHA pin against upstream.
